market_question: Will Marco Rubio win the 2028 US Presidential Election?
reasoning: The 2028 election is nearly five years away, making any single candidate's odds inherently low. Marco Rubio, while a known senator, lost his prior primary bid and lacks the typical frontrunner status (incumbent, VP, or fresh nominee) that justifies a double-digit probability. Historical base rates for similar candidates four years out suggest a true likelihood closer to 6-7%, so the market's 14.1% overstates his chances significantly.
evidence_points: Rubio lost the 2016 Republican primary and has not been a recent presidential nominee.
Open elections without an incumbent typically have widely dispersed candidate odds, with individuals rarely above 10% this early.
Prediction market data from past cycles shows that non-frontrunner candidates with similar profiles historically resolve 'Yes' less than 10% of the time.
sources_consulted: Historical prediction market data for US presidential elections (2004-2020)
Political primary history and election cycle analysis
General knowledge of candidate field and polling averages
